title: Waste, housekeeping and client protection
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: SafeWork NSW, Class B asbestos removal licence (published 12 November 2025; last modified 12 March 2026); Victorian Government (asbestos.vic.gov.au), Unlicensed asbestos removal ('Updated' label shown; no date); WorkSafe Queensland, Asbestos licences (no date shown).
audience: Handyman workers and property maintenance workers working in occupied homes and buildings
learningOutcomes: Prevent trip hazards and protect the occupant's property during a repair.
Control dust so that it does not reach sleeping areas, food or people with breathing conditions.
Segregate controlled waste and stop work when a suspect material is found.

instruction.heading: Protect the occupant and the property
instruction.body: Lay protection before you start, not after. Cover floors, furniture and fittings in the route and in the work area, and keep the route to the work clear of tools, cords and offcuts. Keep a clean path for occupants to move through the property. Protect any food preparation area and any sleeping area from dust. A repair that leaves the property cleaner than before is credible; a repair that leaves dust and debris behind damages trust even when the repair itself is sound.

instruction.heading: Dust, waste and segregation
instruction.body: Separate waste as you go. Use containment and damp methods for dust, and do not dry sweep or use compressed air on dusty material. Keep products away from children and pets, and close containers once used. When material is suspected to contain asbestos, stop disturbing it, keep the area sealed, keep occupants away, and obtain a specialist assessment before any further work. Keep sharps, batteries, solvent and paint waste out of general refuse.

instruction.heading: Stop when a suspect material is found
instruction.body: A repair can expose fibrous fragments, unexpected fine dust, or material that smells or looks different. Stop the disturbing work, keep people clear, and do not sweep or vacuum the suspect material with ordinary equipment. Record what was seen, where, and the steps taken. Refer for a specialist assessment, and tell the approver. Asbestos removal above a state's allowance is licensed work. In New South Wales, a Class B licence applies once the area of non-friable material passes 10 square metres (SafeWork NSW page, published 12 November 2025, modified 12 March 2026). In Victoria, the unlicensed allowance is 10 square metres in total, and one hour in any period of seven days which is cumulative across all employees, for non-friable material only (asbestos.vic.gov.au page, which shows an 'Updated' label and no date). Work above either limit needs a licence. In Queensland, non-friable material at or under 10 square metres needs no licence (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). This lesson does not grant any removal authority.

procedure: Lay floor and furniture protection along the route and around the work area before starting.
Set up containment for dust and identify the route for waste.
Separate waste into general refuse, controlled material and sharps as it is produced.
If fibrous or unexpected material is found, stop disturbing it, keep people clear, and seal the area.
Refer for specialist assessment and record what was seen and the steps taken.
Clean up with damp methods and HEPA-filtered extraction where suitable, and remove all protection at the end.

workedExamples.situation: A repair creates fine dust near a sleeping area, and the worker finds unidentified fibrous fragments in the wall cavity.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the worker continue, sweep up, or stop?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop disturbing the material and keep occupants clear of the sleeping area. Do not dry sweep the fragments. Seal the area, record what was seen, and obtain a specialist assessment before any further work. Continuing or sweeping would spread possible contamination, and it is not a task that this course licenses.

equipmentAndPpe: Floor protection, drop sheets and masking tape
Waste bags and labelled containers for segregated waste
Dust mask or respirator suited to the dust

commonErrors.error: Dry sweeping or using compressed air on dusty or suspect material.
commonErrors.prevention: Use damp methods, and stop when the material is unknown.

commonErrors.error: Putting batteries, solvent waste and sharps into general refuse.
commonErrors.prevention: Segregate waste as it is produced, and check the local waste acceptance rules.

commonErrors.error: Leaving protection up or leaving the route cluttered after the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove protection and clear the route as part of the close-out checklist.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Asbestos: Victoria allows unlicensed removal of non-friable material up to 10 square metres in total, and one hour in any period of seven days which is cumulative across all employees (asbestos.vic.gov.au, which shows an 'Updated' label and no date). Queensland: non-friable material at or under 10 square metres needs no licence (WorkSafe Queensland, no date shown). New South Wales: a Class B licence applies once the area of non-friable material passes 10 square metres (SafeWork NSW, published 12 November 2025, modified 12 March 2026).
Waste acceptance and disposal rules vary by council and state.
Completing this lesson does not give an asbestos removal licence, a waste licence or any authority to remove controlled material.

qualityStandard: Protection is laid before work starts and removed at the end.
Waste is segregated as produced and disposed of under the local rules.
Any suspect material stops the disturbing work and is referred.
documentationEvidence: Waste segregation record with disposal route for each category
Incident note for any suspect material, with the steps taken and the referral
summary: Protect floors, furniture and sleeping areas before starting, and keep the route clear.
Use damp methods and segregate controlled waste as it is produced.
Stop and refer on suspect material, and do not sweep it with ordinary equipment.

knowledgeChecks.question: During a repair, fibrous fragments are found in a wall cavity near a sleeping area. What is the correct action?
options: Continue because the fragments are small, and the room can be used by the occupants again
Sweep them up quickly before they spread through the room and into the hallway for the occupants
Stop disturbing the material, keep occupants clear, seal the area and refer for specialist assessment
Use compressed air to clear the dust from the cavity before the specialist arrives on the site

knowledgeChecks.question: Which waste should not go into general refuse?
Why is dry sweeping of dusty material avoided?
options: It is slower than vacuuming, so it takes longer to finish the job
It damages the floor surface and leaves marks on the boards
It can spread fine dust and possibly hazardous material into the air
The client asks for it not to be done, so the crew must respect that
